children: Investors are increasingly betting on more upside in U.S. Treasurys, according to analysts at The Kobeissi Letter.
The extra cost investors are willing to pay for call options on longer-dated Treasurys
relative to puts has climbed to approximately 50 basis points—the highest level since March 2025.
This marks a sharp reversal from a 250-basis-point premium for puts over calls in late September, The Kobeissi Letter noted.
Treasury prices have been gaining as yields decline. The 10-Year Note Yield
has fallen below 5.00% for the first time since Sept. 23, now down 40 basis points from its Oct. 7 peak.
This suggests investors are increasingly betting on further gains in Treasury prices," the analysts wrote.

The Kobeissi Letter highlighted that one notable options trade is targeting a drop in the 10-Year Note Yield to approximately 4.60% within a month, involving roughly 65,000 contracts and costing around $7 million in premium.
"The bond market is seeing massive swings in price and sentiment," the analysts observed.

title: Investors are betting on U.S. Treasurys as yields rise
